newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ABARE says mixed crop conditions in Australia.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ABARE says mixed crop conditions in Australia.

text.p: Australia's official commodities forecasting agency said on Tuesday favourable weather in New South Wales (NSW) has led to a near ideal finish to an excellent season but conditions have been more varied in other states.

In its state-by-state crop report, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said that while a number of areas across NSW had experienced late problems, above-average yields were expected for most crops.

November rains had led to some harvest delays and heavy storms in the north of the state had caused some crop losses and downgrading, but the impact on total state yields and quality is expected to be relatively minor, ABARE said.

September frosts appeared to have had the most impact on the region north of Coonamble and west of Walgett, producing lower yields and grain sizes there, and indications were for below average protein levels of cereal crops state-wide, it said.

In Victoria, ABARE said the impact on yields was likely to be marginal despite an extended period of below-average rains, although yields in the Mallee region may be slightly below average due to frosts during flowering.
October rains across much of Queensland had disrupted harvesting and led to reports of downgrading of crops in a number of regions, it said.
Recent rains and the late harvest in the south of the state had delayed planting of summer crops, it said.
Harvesting in Western Australia was also delayed by widespread rains in early to mid November.

The rain was not expected to have a large impact on overall quality for most crops, although significant downgrading had been reported in grains in the Geraldton region, and reports of fungal staining in wheat crops, it said.

ABARE said mixed crop conditions had prevailed in South Australia over the spring months, with rainfall well below average in most areas in October and NOvember, although mild conditions limited reductions in yields.
Mid-November rains had not caused any significant crop damage, but further delayed harvest in some areas, which was already two to three weeks later than usual, it said.

The full impact of frosts, mainly in the Murray Mallee region, would not be known until harvesting was well underway, and fine warm conditions were now needed for the majority of the state, ABARE said.
